newsitem.title: UK: British broadcasters link up for digital TV - paper.
newsitem.headline: British broadcasters link up for digital TV - paper.

text.p: British broadcasters Carlton, BSkyB and Granada will announce on Friday that they will jointly bid for the right to launch digital terrestrial television (DTT) in the UK, the Financial Times reported.
The consortium of Carlton Communications, British Sky Broadcasting and the Granada Group will be known as British Digital Broadcasting.
The newspaper said the three companies were also believed to have reached an agreement with the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) to broadcast up to eight subscription channels.
The UK is the first country to announce the launch of DTT, which could take place by the middle of next year.
On Wednesday, the FT reported that BSkyB had decided to press ahead with plans to launch a 200-channel digital satellite service into Britain by late 1997.
